formNote: The simplest graph in the script, a counting stroke, as in 二 and 三. Mojidata IDS treats it as a primitive with no components.
summary: One: the first number, and in early Chinese cosmology the first thing the Way gives rise to. The Shuowen opens its whole dictionary with it.
placement: On the axis above the sphere, at the system's upper equilibrium (x = y = 0, z ≈ 1.943), mirroring 空 at the lower one: the flow turns about the axis that joins them. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

satellites.title: The First Entry of the Shuowen
satellites.evidence: The Shuowen begins with 一 and glosses it as a cosmogony: 惟初太始，道立於一，造分天地，化成萬物 — “in the very beginning, the Way was established in the One, which divided Heaven and Earth and transformed into the myriad things.” A dictionary of the script opens with the beginning of the world.
satellites.caveat: The gloss explains meaning through Han cosmology; it says nothing about the graph’s history.

satellites.title: Attaining the One
satellites.evidence: Daodejing ch. 39: 昔之得一者：天得一以清，地得一以寧 — “of old, those that attained the One: Heaven attained the One and was clear, Earth attained the One and was settled.” Here 一 is less a number than a wholeness each thing depends on.

satellites.title: The One Vehicle
satellites.evidence: 一 renders eka, “one”, in 一乘, ekayāna, the One Vehicle of the Lotus Sutra. Kumārajīva’s verse: 十方佛土中，唯有一乘法，無二亦無三 — “in the Buddha-lands of the ten directions there is only the Dharma of the One Vehicle, not two and not three.”
satellites.caveat: 無二 here means there is no second vehicle; it is not 不二, advaya (see 二’s card). The Lotus counts vehicles; it does not say that all things are one.

checked.note: 十方佛土中，唯有一乘法，無二亦無三。除佛方便說. Checks the Chinese; the Sanskrit is not checked here.
